overview: Find the Blueprints that hold editable settings for menus, character previews, sequencers, and story playback. The related actor pages show how DataTables select a character, summon, trap, effect, weapon, or decal Blueprint.
notes: The Parameter asset type scans the Commons folders for widgets, sequences, and scripts. The game reads these Blueprint class defaults as shared settings.
The wiki documents native setting types, traced code paths, and examples found in the available project assets. Individual values saved in Blueprint packages are outside this coverage.
The mod cook configuration adds `/Game/Mods` to the Parameter scan. See `Config/Custom/JJKModCook/DefaultGame.ini:46`.

entries.title: GameParameterBase and the Parameter primary asset type
entries.overview: This is the common root for Blueprint assets that exist mainly to hold editable game settings.
entries.description: UGameParameterBase is a Blueprintable UObject with no declared properties of its own. The asset manager scans PrimaryAssetType 'Parameter' with this class as AssetBaseClass and bHasBlueprintClasses=True in three Commons directories. Managers load a parameter Blueprint's generated class synchronously through TSoftClassPtr and read its class default object, so the Blueprint's edited defaults act as data for systems that never create an instance of that class. The widget, sequencer and script families documented here are concrete descendants of this root.
notes: The base class itself declares no UPROPERTY; useful fields live in its subclasses and native structs.
The mod configuration adds /Game/Mods to the same Parameter scan (Config/Custom/JJKModCook/DefaultGame.ini:46); no mod asset is documented here.
No serialized defaults are reported: the class default object is the delivery mechanism, but its stored property values were not read from the cooked package.

entries.title: Widget parameter Blueprint defaults
entries.overview: These Blueprints hold the editable defaults that the UI manager reads when the game starts.
entries.description: AGameWidgetManager resolves nine named Blueprint classes under /Game/Widgets/Commons/ and stores their class default objects. Their properties feed the settings screens, key-repeat controller, font cache, dynamic icon lookup, image offsets, scrolling text, story-demo presentation and scene-capture trees. All nine descend from UGameWidgetParameterBase, which descends from UGameParameterBase. The scan also registers them as Parameter primary assets; no separate actor instance is spawned from these classes.

fields.name: ChatParameterMap

fields.technical: EditAnywhere map on UGameWidgetDynamicIconParameter; FindChatParameter and FindChatIconSprite return its category entry or a static default with a null sprite.

fields.simple: Per-character story-demo values.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable map keyed by FName; GetCharacterParameter returns the entry or a default-constructed value.

fields.name: ScrollMaterial
fields.simple: Material used by scrolling text.
fields.technical: BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere pointer; GameWidgetTextScroll creates a dynamic material instance from it for the text and outline fonts.

fields.simple: Horizontal and vertical scroll speed.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable 2D vector read by FGameWidgetTextScroll when advancing scrolled text.

notes: Only the nine named class paths are loaded by AGameWidgetManager; other similarly named native classes without such a loader are not given a page here.
Property types come from native headers. The edited values in each Blueprint's class default object were not serialized or inferred.
Find* helpers in these classes return static default-constructed values when a map key is missing, so absence of an entry is not the same as a zero value.

entries.title: Character and capture-type scene-capture parameters
entries.overview: These Blueprints supply the camera, light and character-presentation defaults used by UI character captures.
entries.description: GameWidgetSceneCaptureParameter_BP is the root parameter Blueprint loaded by AGameWidgetManager. Its native class holds maps pointing to per-capture-type and per-character parameter Blueprints under /Game/Widgets/Commons/Parameters/, plus an array of render targets. Those referenced Blueprints derive from UGameWidgetSceneCaptureTypeParameter or UGameWidgetCharacterSceneCaptureParameter. GameWidgetManager resolves the maps through the root object's class default object and passes the resulting structs into the character-capture actor; it never spawns an instance of the parameter classes themselves.

fields.simple: Camera and light settings for each capture type.

fields.name: CameraParameter
fields.simple: Where the capture camera sits and how it renders.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable struct on UGameWidgetSceneCaptureTypeParameter. Its members include CameraFov (float), Transform (FTransform), ImageSize (FIntPoint), PanelActorBP (TSubclassOf<AGameCharacterCapturePanelActor>), PanelTransform (FTransform) and CaptureSource (TEnumAsByte<ESceneCaptureSource>).

fields.name: LightParameter
fields.simple: Lighting used for a capture type.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable struct with Transform (FTransform), bUsePointLight (bool), PointLightAttenuation (FVector) and PointLightColor (FLinearColor). Its constructor copies static native defaults.

fields.name: ParameterMap
fields.simple: Per-capture settings inside one character Blueprint.
fields.technical: EditAnywhere map on UGameWidgetCharacterSceneCaptureParameter; the root class indexes it by the widget capture type before reading common or costume variation values.

fields.name: CommonParameter
fields.simple: Shared outline, mask and transform values for a character capture.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable struct containing fields such as OutlineWidth, TranslucentScale, DecalDissolvePattern (int32), DecalDissolveWeight, CharacterLightShadowColor (FLinearColor), Transform, ShikigamiTransform, AnimationWeaponTransformMap (TMap<FName,FTransform>), MaskRange and MaskEdgeFalloff (FVector4).

fields.name: VariationParameterMap
fields.simple: Costume-specific overrides for a character capture.
fields.technical: EditAnywhere map inside FGameWidgetCharacterSceneCaptureTypeParameter. Values carry MaterialPattern (int32), BackgroundColor (EGameWidgetCaptureBackgroundColor), BackgroundColorDetails, ToneCurveAmount, AlphaExp, Mask, CutOffMax and CutOffMin floats.

notes: The reference relationships were observed in the root Blueprint package name table, which lists the per-character and capture-type package paths; their stored map values were not decoded.
No catalog data-table group was established as the backing store for this Blueprint tree; the CharacterCapture* catalog groups describe separate row data.

The per-character parameter packages name their native parent class but do not expose a generated _C class string in their name tables; they are described from the native parent and their location in the Parameter scan.

entries.title: Sequencer loading and offset parameters
entries.overview: These Blueprints tell the sequencer which level sequences to collect and how to shift global positions.
entries.description: AGameSequencerManager's BootInitialize loads two named Parameter Blueprints from /Game/Sequences/Commons/ with the same soft-class-to-CDO pattern used by the widget manager. GameSequencerLoadingParameter_BP owns an array of per-sequence file descriptors used when collecting animation, decal, texture and NPC assets. GameSequencerOffsetParameter_BP owns a name-keyed map of global offset locations. Both are Blueprintable UGameParameterBase descendants and are scanned by the Parameter primary asset type.

examples.name: GameSequencerLoadingParameter_BP
examples.detail: Array of per-sequence file parameters read during boot and sequence collection.

examples.name: GameSequencerOffsetParameter_BP
examples.detail: Name-to-offset map queried by the sequencer manager.

fields.name: FileParameters
fields.simple: One entry per level sequence the game may load.
fields.technical: BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere array on UGameSequencerLoadingParameter. Each element has ID and Filename (FName), bKeepLighting and bKeepFacial (bool), BindingSupportCharacterIdMap and BindingWeaponIdMap (TMap<FName,FName>), and arrays of animation, decal, texture and NPC reference structs.

fields.name: SettingsMap
fields.simple: Offsets for named sequence locations.
fields.technical: BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere map on UGameSequencerOffsetParameter. FindGlobalOffsetLocation looks up a name and returns the entry's OffsetLocation, or nullptr for an unknown key; the caller does not null-test the resulting pointer.

fields.name: OffsetLocation
fields.simple: World-space displacement for a named offset.
fields.technical: Sole property of FGameSequencerGlobalOffsetParameter, exposed BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere.

notes: The page covers two distinct native roots; baseClass names the loading parameter class because it has the larger editable structure.
UGameSequencerRetargetingParameter is Blueprintable in native code but no matching Blueprint package was observed locally, so it is not given an example here.
Sequence file descriptors are not the same assets as the Script primary asset type or the catalog's sequence-related data-table groups; no table group is asserted for these parameters.

entries.title: Script playback parameter Blueprint
entries.overview: This single Blueprint controls timing and audio ducking defaults for scripted scenes.
entries.description: GameScriptPlayer loads /Game/Scripts/Commons/GameScriptParameter_BP as a UGameScriptParameter class and shares its class default object with the script context. Script commands read its auto-wait times and ducking values directly when showing messages, waiting for input and starting BGM ducking. The Blueprint is a Parameter primary asset; it is distinct from the Script primary asset type, which uses non-Blueprint UGameScriptData assets for the script content itself.

examples.name: GameScriptParameter_BP
examples.detail: Only parameter Blueprint observed in /Game/Scripts/Commons; loaded by GameScriptPlayer.

fields.name: DefaultAutoWaitTime
fields.simple: How long a script step waits when no other timing is given.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float exposed by GetDefaultAutoWaitTime; WaitInput::Start and message steps read it as their initial remaining time.

fields.name: MessageAutoWaitTime
fields.simple: Extra wait after a message line.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float read by message commands as MessageWaitTime.

fields.name: VoiceAutoWaitTime
fields.simple: Wait used while a voice line plays.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float chosen instead of the default wait when a command has voices.

fields.name: DuckingVolume
fields.simple: BGM level during scripted ducking.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float multiplied by the current BGM volume when starting a duck.

fields.name: DuckingFadeTime
fields.simple: How long the BGM duck takes.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float used as the ducking duration and also compared with the script's delay.

fields.name: DuckingEasingType
fields.simple: Easing curve used for the volume duck.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable enum property passed into the BGM ducking start call.

fields.name: DuckingBlendExp
fields.simple: Exponent for the ducking easing curve.
fields.technical: Blueprint-editable float passed as the blend exponent when the ducking helper starts.

notes: The Script primary asset type scans UGameScriptData assets under /Game/Scripts (Config/DefaultGame.ini:30), not this Blueprint; the two are loaded through different paths.
No script-data content is treated as a property default of this Blueprint.

entries.title: Rich-text image decorator Blueprint
entries.overview: This Blueprint gives inline tags in game text their pictures.
entries.description: The TextDecorator primary asset type scans Blueprint classes derived from UGameWidgetRichTextBlockDecoratorBase in /Game/Widgets/Commons/. The observed BP_RichTextBlockdecorator derives from UGameWidgetRichTextBlockDecorator and assigns a DataTable as CustomImageSet. When rich text encounters an tag, FindImageBrush uses the tag or id directly as a row name and returns that row's Slate brush. This is a Blueprint-backed decorator object, not a UGameParameterBase settings Blueprint.

examples.name: BP_RichTextBlockdecorator
examples.detail: Decorator Blueprint whose package imports GameWidgetRichTextBlockDecorator and RichTextBlockImageDataTable.

fields.name: CustomImageSet
fields.simple: Table that maps image tags to pictures.
fields.technical: Protected BlueprintReadWrite/EditAnywhere pointer on UGameWidgetRichTextBlockDecorator. FindImageBrush calls FindRow<FGameWidgetRichTextBlockImageRow>(TagOrId, FString(), false) on it and returns the row's Brush or nullptr.

notes: The configured scan base is the abstract UGameWidgetRichTextBlockDecoratorBase; the observed Blueprint's direct native parent is the concrete UGameWidgetRichTextBlockDecorator.
Only the discussed table/row relationship is asserted; no default brush values were decoded from the Blueprint or its DataTable.

entries.title: Character actor Blueprints
entries.overview: These Blueprints set up the fighter actors the game spawns, including their meshes, collisions, and controllers.
entries.description: AssetManager scans Character primary assets from GameCharacter_BP and the listed character folders with bHasBlueprintClasses=True. A data-table row supplies FileName_BP, which is turned into a Character primary asset id; the loaded UClass is then spawned as an AGameCharacter. Their native class exposes mesh, collision and controller references, so the Blueprint's edited values configure an actor instance rather than a CDO-only settings object.
